Hi Elena — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we have a single place to track: 

Summary of DataMuse needs (as discussed)

- Avg request: ~420 tokens; 95th pct <= 1,200 tokens.
- Volume estimate: 3.2M tokens/day (average) with 10x burst headroom during peak syncs.
- Latency target: p95 < 350ms for interactive flows.
- Security: SOC 2 required; potential EU data residency for a subset of customers later this year.
- Preference: keep integration simple (hosted API) if cost and SLA are acceptable; otherwise evaluate Dedicated pool or Private VPC for strict tenancy and network controls.

What I promised to do
- Put together three pricing sketches: Hosted (per-token), Dedicated reserved-commit (monthly/annual), and Private VPC (license + infra). See attached "Redwood_TCO_sketch.xlsx" for the first-pass numbers.
- Draft a short mutual action plan for a 2–4 week pilot (attached: "Mutual_Action_Plan_DataMuse.docx").
- Start SOC 2 evidence handoff; Elena, I copied procurement for any immediate docs.

Questions / asks for your team (helps us tighten the pricing):
1) Can you confirm the % of requests that expect <512 tokens vs >512 tokens? (we used 65/35 split in the model)
2) How long do you expect to retain raw input/outputs? (affects storage + audit log sizing)
3) Are there any hard constraints on outbound IP ranges for a Private VPC trial?

Proposed next steps
- Internal: Redwood will circulate a short cost comparison + recommended pilot configuration by EOD PST.
- External: Elena / procurement to confirm interest in 2-week Dedicated pilot or preference to do hosted evaluation first.
- Schedule a demo of the Observability console once pilot config is agreed.

Thanks — I added Soojin (SE) to the thread to provide sizing and a quick back-of-envelope breakeven between per-token hosted and a small Dedicated pool.

Marcus — thanks, good summary. A few notes for pricing / procurement that I'll add to the deck: 

High-level pricing scenarios to prepare (we'll refine with SE numbers)
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token blended rate with optional committed spend credit. Good for low-to-medium sustained volume; fastest time-to-value.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commit for a fixed GPU pool. We surface expected QPS and effective per-token cost in the spreadsheet. Best for predictable mid-to-high sustained throughput.
- Private VPC (enterprise): platform/license + infra + support. Applied when data residency / network isolation is a must. Typically higher fixed cost but lower marginal token cost if usage is high.

Specific asks for SE (So we can produce a clean breakeven):
- Confirm concurrency distribution (avg concurrent requests during peak 1h window).
- Typical model/quality target (we used an LlamaX-7B-equivalent profile with 8k KV cache in the sketch).
- Expected evaluation dataset (number of eval prompts) so we can size logging & eval storage.

If procurement is going to push for committed pricing, note we usually provide graded discounts for 6/12/24 month commits. Also can offer a small pilot credit against a committed contract if they convert.

I'll hold a short slide with the three scenarios and clear callouts: runway to breakeven, operational tradeoffs, and recommended pilot configuration.

- Lauren

Looping in a quick SE back-of-envelope based on Marcus' call notes and the spreadsheet: 

Assumptions I used (call + Marcus spreadsheet)
- Avg tokens/request: 420 (65% <512, 35% between 512-1200)
- Avg model latency target: p95 < 350ms
- Sustained tokens/day: 3.2M (peak burst factor 8x for short windows)
- Model family: LlamaX-7B-ish performance for recompute; KV cache enabled.

Rough pricing breakeven (very approximate)
- Hosted per-token blended rate (our estimate for that workload): $0.00055 / token effective. At 3.2M tokens/day -> ~$1,760/day -> ~$53k/month.
- Small Dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalent reserved) effective cost after a modest 12-month commit discount: ~ $35k/month (includes instance + infra premium). Breakeven ~1.7M tokens/day at that model profile.
- Private VPC (license + infra): ~ $55k-$75k/month baseline depending on customer-managed infra; marginal cost per-token then drops materially for very high volume (10M tokens/day+).

Implication: for DataMuse's current volume estimate (3.2M tokens/day) the Dedicated reserved option is likely cheaper than Hosted if they are comfortable with a 6–12 month commit; Hosted is simpler and carries no infra responsibility but is ~30–50% more expensive at current run rate in my sketch. Private VPC only makes sense if you need strong tenancy/data residency or expect a 3x+ increase in sustained volume.

Pilot proposal (for the MAP)
- Option A (recommended pilot path): 2-week Dedicated trial (1–2 reserved GPUs equivalent) with our metrics hooks enabled + SLO dashboard. We can apply a $5k pilot credit that would be deducted from a 12-month conversion.
- Option B (low-friction): 2-week Hosted trial using committed credits (no infra changes) — faster but won't prove autoscaling behavior under sustained load.

Next steps I need from Marcus / procurement
- Approval to offer a 12-month committed pricing tier draft and to include a $5k pilot credit if they sign within 30 days.
- Confirmation on the token size distribution and retention window so I can finalize the cost rows.

Happy to jump on a short call with DataMuse SE/procurement to walk the numbers through.

—Soojin
